title: Deterministic SSE finalization via chunk-sealing and replay tokens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Several customers reported truncated or duplicated text after abrupt SSE disconnects when traffic traversed mix of Hosted routing and Dedicated backends. Existing reconnect heuristics can leave the final user-visible message in an indeterminate state (missing tail tokens or repeated fragments). This ticket adds a deterministic finalization protocol for multipart SSE sessions: server-side chunk sealing plus short-lived replay tokens so clients and edge proxies can request exact replay ranges and detect when a session is fully finalized. The goal is to eliminate user-visible holes and make replays idempotent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a sealed-chunk marker that is emitted as the last event for a finalized segment; clients must be able to detect 'sealed' and treat subsequent reconnects as either continuation or new session.
Provide a lightweight replay token (opaque, HMAC-signed) for each sealed chunk containing start_offset and end_offset so clients can request deterministic replay of missing ranges within 60s.
No visible duplication or missing tokens in production Canary (15k live streaming sessions) for 72 hours after rollout compared to baseline error rate.

Fallbacks: if replay token verification fails or server state is unavailable, clients receive clear error event and SDK performs exponential backoff with user-facing guidance rather than re-emitting partial tokens.
Feature works for cross-routing scenarios: Hosted->Dedicated handoff and Dedicated->Hosted fallback preserve chunk sealing semantics.
E2E tests that assert idempotent reconstructions on artificial mid-stream TCP resets for both JSON streaming and text-plain SSE consumers.
technical_design: Design notes: implement a short-lived session ledger entry per streaming request stored in the existing in-memory shard (Redis cluster used by serving runtime) with keys: session_id -> [sealed_segments metadata] and a monotonic token-offset counter. When runtime flushes a segment it emits an SSE 'sealed' event with an HMAC-signed replay token (base64). The token encodes session_id, segment_end_offset, and expiry. On reconnect, client exchanges last-seen-offset; if server detects offset < sealed_end it issues a replay of [offset, sealed_end] using server-side reassembly. For Dedicated/private deployments where ephemeral state may be on remote GPUs, we replicate sealed metadata to central control-plane for at least token expiry window. To minimize perf impact, sealing occurs only on segment boundaries (every N tokens or on completion), and token generation is async-offloaded to the runtime worker.
implementation_steps: Add 'sealed' SSE event type to the streaming protocol spec and update internal proto definitions
Runtime: persist sealed-segment metadata (session_id, start_offset, end_offset, hmac_token) into Redis with 60s TTL
Runtime: add HMAC signing endpoint that uses service key and rotates keys every 24h; implement token format and verification logic
Edge: update Hosted edge to forward client reconnects with last_seen_offset header and optional replay_token header

SDKs: (JS and Python) add logic to detect 'sealed' events, store replay_token, and on reconnect call '/stream/replay?token=...&offset=...'. Provide safe-backoff and user-visible guidance if replay not possible
Dedicated: extend control-plane agent to mirror sealed metadata into customers' control-plane endpoint for Private deployments; add flag for customers to opt-in to 60s replicated ledger
Add integration tests that simulate mid-stream TCP resets and assert deterministic reassembly
Run canary in Hosted with 5% traffic, monitor duplication/missing-token metrics and latency regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding and HMAC verification
Mock runtime tests: create synthetic streams that seal at irregular boundaries and validate replay results
Chaos test: orchestrate abrupt session kill at random offsets across a fleet of 200 streaming clients and assert reconstructed outputs match golden transcripts
Load test: ensure additional Redis ops and token signing latency do not increase P50/P95 token emit latency beyond 5ms budget
Canary plan: start with internal traffic (10k sessions), then 5% external traffic for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours before full rollout
rollout_plan: Feature flag gating: runtime and SDK changes behind 'sse_chunk_sealing' flag
Canary 0 -> internal dev tenants (2026-03-14), if stable enable 5% Hosted traffic (2026-03-16)
Monitor duplication/missing_token and 'replay_failures' dashboards; require <0.1% replay_failures and no client-visible regression
If metrics stable after 48h, expand to 25% then 100% over a week
Coordinate Dedicated rollout with account owners: enable ledger replication during scheduled maintenance windows
rollback_plan: Gate via config: disable 'sse_chunk_sealing' flag on runtime and edge will revert to previous reconnect behavior. For Dedicated/customers who enabled ledger replication, rotate off replication and TTL will naturally expire stored metadata. SDKs will ignore sealed events when flag is disabled.
notes: Customer escalations: AcmeDocs reported repeated missing trailing sentences after a reconnect on 2026-01-28 (support ticket #ACME-418). They are cadence-critical and blocked on hosted fix.

Design tradeoff: sealing introduces small metadata writes per segment; we tuned TTL to 60s to bound operational cost while supporting typical reconnect windows. Longer TTL increases storage and complexity for Dedicated mirrors.
Security: tokens are HMAC-signed and short-lived; we avoid embedding raw content in tokens to prevent data leakage.
Related: this approach differs from naive re-streaming because it guarantees server-authored boundaries and idempotent replays across heterogeneous routing paths.
